key_insight: This paper introduces "Sustainability Robotics" as a new discipline that unifies robotics research around environmental and societal goals. It proposes a shared framework to reduce fragmentation and guide both greener robot design and the use of robots to support sustainability.
problem_solved: Robotics research is often fragmented across subfields, making it harder to coordinate efforts toward meaningful sustainability outcomes. The paper addresses the lack of a common discipline-level vision for aligning robotics with sustainability goals.
method: Defines Sustainability Robotics as a new umbrella discipline for connecting robotics innovation with sustainability impact.
Proposes three guiding principles to steer research, design, and deployment decisions.
Introduces two dimensions of the field: sustainable design and robotics for sustainability.
impact: For AI/ML and robotics practitioners, this provides a clearer roadmap for building systems that are not only technically advanced but also environmentally and socially responsible. It can help teams evaluate research directions, design choices, and application targets through a sustainability lens.
visual_elements: A 2D matrix showing the two dimensions: sustainable design vs. robotics for sustainability
A three-part principle icon set summarizing the guiding principles
A pipeline diagram showing how robotics research connects to sustainability outcomes
Icons for energy, materials, environment, and society to represent impact areas
paper_authors: S. Song, B. Mazzolai, M. Kovač
